newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Stora considers mills in Asia, South America.
newsitem.headline: Stora considers mills in Asia, South America.

text.p: Swedish forestry group Stora AB said on Thursday it was considering starting fine paper production in Southeast Asia and pulp production in South America.

These ideas, along with continued expansion of sales resources in Southeast Asia, are part of a possible longterm scenario, chief executive Lars-Ake Helgesson said at the annual general shareholders' meeting, according to a statement.

"A prerequisite for the production of fine papers in Southeast Asia, however, is that we first ensure access to longterm and assured supplies of short fibre pulp, since this is the key to low production costs," he said. "That is why pulp production must come first."
Stora is studying various alternatives for pulp production in Southeast Asia and South America, but favours the latter.

"Thus, a wholly, or partly owned pulp mill, in South America is the key that will subsequently enable Stora to start up, in some form, the group's own fine paper production in Southeast Asia," Helgesson said.
Regarding market conditions, Helgesson said the inventory reduction phase is over for most of Stora's products, with the exception of pulp.

"Combined with the positive trend for the European economies, this should lead to increased deliveries," Helgesson said, adding the upturn would be slow. Stora also expected product prices to turn up this year, albeit slowly.
"There is no guarantee that average prices will achieve higher levels in 1997 than in 1996," he said. "The inventory trend for pulp will play an important role in this regard."
If the current development of sterling and dollar -- which are important for Stora -- continues, it will have a positive effect on company earnings, Helgesson added.
